subclaim: S4 (drift of the error with the split draw) and Remark F-3 (rem:designs): only a jointly scored block K-fold fixes the scored population
origem: pre-submission check adopted on 03/10/2026: test E1, requested in the internal review of the manuscript
pergunta: For the constant predictor and the calibrated FSPL, does a jointly scored block K-fold (each node scored once, in the fold in which it is held out) eliminate or reduce the between-draw drift of the error on the valid nodes and on all nodes, with and without buffer, compared with the block hold-out with buffer on the held-out side (8.0 dB between split draws versus 2.2 dB between cells)?
desenho: 16 cells; the same 60 split draws (split_seed) of fase2/2.1_deriva_erro_baselines_16x60rnd.json; blocks of g = 10 km by the same block function of the project (SpatialKFold._assign_groups); in each split draw the block permutation (RandomState(split_seed)) is cut into K = 6 folds of equal size (22 blocks; the hold-out test set has k_te = 20), not into 92/20/20; for each fold as held out: (i) without buffer (b = 0): all nodes of the fold scored; (ii) with buffer on the held-out side (b = 2 km): fold nodes less than 2 km from any node outside the fold are removed (same trimming rule as the hold-out, cKDTree); prediction: constant = median of the training nodes (the other 5 folds, sentinels included, as in 2.1); calibrated FSPL (b) = offset by the median of the valid training nodes of the other 5 folds; Err_conjunto(sigma) = MAE over the union of the nodes scored in the 6 folds, per population (valid; all); also record the fraction of nodes scored and the number of valid nodes scored per split draw.
metricas: per cell, predictor, population and b: SD (ddof=1) across the 60 split draws of Err_conjunto; mean; SD across the means of the 16 cells; ratio dp_sorteios_medio / dp_entre_celulas (same simple convention as T.dp_sorteio / T.dp_entre_medias); ratio of the between-draw SD of the joint K-fold to the between-draw SD of the hold-out (T.dp_sorteio = 8.02 dB for constant/valid/b = 2, and U.* for b = 0); mean bias of Err_conjunto against the domain mean (mu_U of 2.1/R2) per cell.
leitura: Constant, valid, b = 0: the population is fixed by construction, so SD = 0 exactly (control: if it does not give 0, the loop is wrong). Constant, valid, b = 2: if the ratio dp_sorteios/dp_entre_celulas is < 1 in >= 12 of the 16 cells AND the mean between-draw SD is < 1/4 of the hold-out (< 2.0 dB) -> REINFORCES F-3 and the text gains the practical recommendation ('when the target is the domain mean, score the folds jointly; the hold-out is the protocol in which the drift appears'), and the title claim stays delimited to the hold-out (which is what the title says). If the between-draw SD with b = 2 is >= 1/2 of the hold-out in >= 8 cells -> DELIMITS F-3: the buffer on the held-out side reintroduces composition drift even in the joint K-fold; the text states this as a condition and does not recommend the K-fold without qualification. In between: descriptive, one sentence with the numbers. Calibrated FSPL: reported alongside, without a rule (per-fold calibration introduces its own variation).
se_inverter: no outcome inverts the title (which is about the hold-out); the worst outcome is the absence of a practical recommendation.
orcamento: CPU; 16 cells x 60 split draws x 6 folds x 2 values of b; estimate: 2-4 h in the s33 venv with the per-cell partial results; no GPU.
